mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and slower economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate profits.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and economic growth are expected to be robust.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate fiscal stimulus.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a weakening supply side, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate profits.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.
